metadata.title: ORCHID examples: runnable workflows on the ORCHID data (PhaseForge+, ESPEI, one-shot MLIP phase diagrams, MLIP formation enthalpies, quickstart)
metadata.description:
ORCHID examples: runnable, documented examples of the workflows described in the ORCHID paper: tuning an MLIP-informed Cu-Zr CALPHAD description with gradient-based ESPEI against ORCHID data (PhaseForge+), the classic ESPEI MCMC route as a documented negative example, prevalence-weighted scoring of one-shot MLIP phase diagrams against ORCHID evidence, the saturation of MLIP formation-enthalpy accuracy at the DFT level, PhaseForge input structures, and a quickstart notebook. Cached examples can be inspected without rerunning the expensive calculations, while full model generation and fitting require the dependencies and resources documented for each workflow. Each example pins the ORCHID release commit and its software versions. Software record of release v2026.10; the data it uses are in the ORCHID data records (umbrella: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23736065).

Contents: 426 files (13,931 kB), the git archive of commit 6d68789772 of github.com/orchid-calphad/orchid-examples. The archive is built from the commit recorded in its manifest; reproduction results apply only to the tested commit and the documented cached paths.

Licence

Code (all .py and .sh files, notebook code cells, CI workflow): MIT (LICENSE). Data in the repository keep the licences of their sources (LICENSE-DATA.md): values derived from ORCHID and the SGTE TDB files are CC BY 4.0, with attribution to the ORCHID release and to Hallstedt (2025). The record's licence field states the code licence (MIT).

Limitations

  • Cached outputs are small summaries; the bulky raw outputs of the full runs are not part of this record.
  • Refined Cu-Zr TDBs are review-only demonstration models, not assessments.

How to cite

R. Arróyave, J. Saal, D. Shin, ORCHID examples: runnable workflows on the ORCHID data (PhaseForge+, ESPEI, one-shot MLIP phase diagrams, MLIP formation enthalpies, quickstart) (version 2026.10), Zenodo (2026). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23736043. Please also cite the ORCHID data release you used, the ORCHID paper, the software each example credits and the original sources of the data.

Software and data citations

These credits describe the ORCHID project and its examples. Cite the papers and software used in your analysis, together with the ORCHID release and original source of each observation. The list does not imply that every dataset was generated with every package. Preserve the versions and commit hashes recorded by each example; a repository link is not a reproducibility pin. Materials Project and OQMD energies retain separate references.

  • pycalphad: Thermodynamic calculations and phase equilibria. R. Otis and Z.-K. Liu (2017), pycalphad: CALPHAD-based Computational Thermodynamics in Python (10.5334/jors.140). Repository.
  • ESPEI: Thermodynamic parameter fitting and uncertainty quantification. B. Bocklund et al. (2019), ESPEI for efficient thermodynamic database development, modification, and uncertainty quantification: application to Cu–Mg (10.1557/mrc.2019.59). Repository.
  • PhaseForge: MLIP-informed CALPHAD construction in the examples. S. Zhu, D. Sarıtürk, and R. Arróyave (2025), Machine learning potentials for alloys: a detailed workflow to predict phase diagrams and benchmark accuracy (10.1038/s41524-025-01814-z). Repository; archived software.
  • PhaseForge+: Construction and experimental tuning of CALPHAD models in the examples; repository name PhaseForgePlus. C. Kunselman, S. Zhu, D. Sarıtürk, and R. Arróyave (2025), Construction and Tuning of CALPHAD Models Using Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials and Experimental Data: A Case Study of the Pt–W System (10.1007/s11669-025-01222-2). Repository; archived software.
  • Materials Project: DFT structures and energies; repository link is the API client, not the database itself. A. Jain et al. (2013), Commentary: The Materials Project: A materials genome approach to accelerating materials innovation (10.1063/1.4812323). Repository; data resource.
  • OQMD: DFT structures and energies; qmpy is the supporting software. J. E. Saal et al. (2013), Materials Design and Discovery with High-Throughput Density Functional Theory: The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD) (10.1007/s11837-013-0755-4); S. Kirklin et al. (2015), The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD): assessing the accuracy of DFT formation energies (10.1038/npjcompumats.2015.10). Repository; data resource.
